title: `build_pipeline` builds profiles for hmm queries in parallel
body:
`build_pipeline` in `search.rs` builds the query profiles. For sequence queries it uses `par_iter()`. For hmm queries it calls `p7hmm.iter()`, with the `par_iter()` version commented out on the line above. On the mgy run the pipeline build takes 6.2 s, 1.3% of the run and the second largest serial item. Most of that is likely the serial parse of 20,795 Pfam profiles.

## Proposal

Restore the `par_iter()` line, after checking that the race recorded with commit `3a964e5` is fixed. The note on that commit has the details.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text: On the mgy run pipeline build is 6.2 s, 1.3% of the run, the second largest serial item. Blocked on the libsail evaluation since it may replace the p7hmm parsing this touches.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/2aff5e6c
notes.text: Commit `3a964e5` commented out the `par_iter()` line in `search.rs`, with the message "It was a race condition on file handles." The same commit rewrote `Database` in `database.rs` and its rayon impl in `impl_rayon.rs`, and `dev.rs` uses `p7hmm.par_iter()` today. The commented line looks like a leftover from debugging that race. Nobody has checked that the fixed `Database` is safe for it. The libsail evaluation closed without touching this, since the fix changes no parsing code.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text:
Restored `p7hmm.par_iter()` in `build_pipeline`. A full run of 20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 targets at `-t 8` took the pipeline build from 3.07 s to 0.40 s, and setup from 6.52 s to 1.45 s. Both runs wrote 3,031,623 lines to `results.tbl`. The two files are identical once sorted, and their row order differs from line 4 on.

The row order does not come from this change. On 300 Pfam profiles against the first 50,000 mgy targets, the serial build and the parallel build each ran three times at `-t 8`. All six files differ byte for byte and are identical once sorted. At `-t 1`, two runs of each build are byte-identical to each other and to one another. The serial build reorders rows too, so the order varies with the thread count, not with how the profiles are parsed. The race recorded with `3a964e5` would show up as changed rows, and no row changed.
